title: Closed Interval Merge
prompt:
Implement `merge_intervals(intervals) -> list[list[int]]` for closed integer intervals `[start, end]`. Sort the intervals by start, then merge an interval into the preceding result exactly when its start is at most the preceding end. In particular, `[4, 5]` and `[5, 8]` share the closed endpoint 5 and merge, whereas `[2, 4]` and `[5, 7]` remain separate.

Return merged intervals in increasing start order. An empty input returns an empty list. The input may be unsorted and may contain nested or repeated intervals.

example.reasoning: The first two closed intervals overlap, while the last interval is disjoint.
